items.subject: math
items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (2x³)²?
items.explanation: Square each factor: 2² = 4 and (x³)² = x⁶ because the exponents multiply. So (2x³)² = 4x⁶.

commonErrors.why: Added the exponents 3 + 2 instead of multiplying them.
Made both errors: did not square the 2 and added the exponents.
Squared the x³ but forgot to square the coefficient 2.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Evaluate (2⁵ × 2⁻²) ÷ 2⁻¹.
items.explanation: Subtract exponents when dividing and add when multiplying: 5 + (−2) − (−1) = 4, so the value is 2⁴ = 16.

commonErrors.why: Subtracted 1 instead of subtracting −1, getting 2² = 4.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Simplify (6a⁴b⁻²)² ÷ (4a⁻¹b³) and write it with positive exponents.
items.explanation: Square first: 36a⁸b⁻⁴. Divide: 36 ÷ 4 = 9, a⁸⁻⁽⁻¹⁾ = a⁹, b⁻⁴⁻³ = b⁻⁷. So the result is 9a⁹/b⁷.

commonErrors.why: Subtracted the a-exponents as 8 − 1 instead of 8 − (−1).
Doubled the 6 instead of squaring it, so the coefficient became 12 rather than 36.
Combined the b-exponents as −4 + 3 instead of −4 − 3.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A school club orders custom T-shirts. The total cost in dollars for n shirts is 12n + 40. What does the 40 represent?
items.explanation: 12n changes with the number of shirts, so 12 is the price per shirt. The 40 is added no matter what n is, so it is a fixed one-time fee.
choices: A one-time design fee that does not depend on n
items.answer: A one-time design fee that does not depend on n

commonErrors.why: Read 12 and 40 as one combined quantity instead of separate parts.
Confused the constant with the coefficient of n, which is the per-shirt price.
Treated the constant as the input variable n.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: In the expression 5x² − 3x + 7, what is the coefficient of the x term?
items.explanation: The x term is −3x, so its coefficient is −3, including the sign.

commonErrors.why: Used the coefficient of the x² term.
Used the constant term.
Dropped the negative sign in front of the term.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: An account balance after t years is modeled by 500(1.04)ᵗ. Which statement correctly names the parts of this expression?
items.explanation: In a(b)ᵗ, a = 500 multiplies the power (the coefficient), b = 1.04 is the base, and t in the superscript is the exponent.
choices: 500 is the coefficient, 0.04 is the base, and t is the exponent
500 is the base, 1.04 is the exponent, and t is the coefficient
1.04 is the coefficient, 500 is the base, and t is the exponent
500 is the coefficient, 1.04 is the base, and t is the exponent
items.answer: 500 is the coefficient, 1.04 is the base, and t is the exponent

commonErrors.answer: 500 is the coefficient, 0.04 is the base, and t is the exponent
commonErrors.why: Used only the growth rate 0.04 as the base instead of 1.04.

commonErrors.answer: 500 is the base, 1.04 is the exponent, and t is the coefficient
commonErrors.why: Mixed up which part sits in the exponent position.

commonErrors.answer: 1.04 is the coefficient, 500 is the base, and t is the exponent
commonErrors.why: Swapped the coefficient and the base.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A student buys n notebooks that cost $3 each and one backpack that costs b dollars. The store takes 10% off the whole order, so the total paid is 0.9(3n + b). What does the part 3n + b represent?
items.explanation: Inside the parentheses, 3n is the notebook cost and b is the backpack cost. Their sum is the pre-discount total, which 0.9 then reduces.
choices: The cost of the notebooks only
The total the student pays after the discount
The amount of money taken off by the discount
The cost of all the items before the discount
items.answer: The cost of all the items before the discount

commonErrors.answer: The cost of the notebooks only
commonErrors.why: Ignored the backpack term b.

commonErrors.answer: The total the student pays after the discount
commonErrors.why: Forgot that the factor 0.9 is what applies the discount.

commonErrors.answer: The amount of money taken off by the discount
commonErrors.why: Mistook the sum inside the parentheses for the discount amount, which would be 0.1(3n + b).

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Kai has P dollars in an account, deposits $50 more, and then earns 8% interest on the whole balance, so the new balance is 1.08(P + 50). This equals (P + 50) + 0.08(P + 50). Which part is the interest Kai earns?
items.explanation: The balance before interest is P + 50. The interest is 8% of that balance, 0.08(P + 50), and the full balance is that balance plus its interest.

commonErrors.why: Used the original balance after interest, which is not the interest alone.
Applied the interest only to the original P and left out the $50 deposit.
Used the balance before interest was added.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The function f(x) = x² − 5x + 6 can be factored. What are all of the zeros of f?
items.explanation: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3). Setting each factor to 0 gives x = 2 and x = 3.

commonErrors.why: Read the zeros straight from the coefficients.
Chose a factor pair of 6 that does not add to −5.
Used the factor numbers without reversing the signs in (x − 2)(x − 3).

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Which is the factored form of 2x² + 7x + 3?
items.explanation: (2x + 1)(x + 3) = 2x² + 6x + x + 3 = 2x² + 7x + 3, so the middle term matches.

commonErrors.why: Used negative constants, giving 2x² − 7x + 3.
Mixed the signs, giving 2x² − 5x − 3.
Placed the factors of 3 in the wrong positions, giving 2x² + 5x + 3.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The function g(x) = 6x² + 7x − 20 factors as (3x − 4)(2x + 5). What is its positive zero? Enter a fraction or decimal.
items.explanation: Set 3x − 4 = 0 to get x = 4/3. The other zero from 2x + 5 = 0 is x = −5/2, which is negative.

commonErrors.why: Used the size of the negative zero, forgetting its sign.
Inverted the fraction when solving 3x − 4 = 0.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Multiply (2x + 3)(x − 5) and write the result as ax² + bx + c. What is the value of b?

commonErrors.why: Used only the outer product and forgot to combine with 3x.
Subtracted 3x from −10x instead of adding.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Simplify (5x² − 3x + 4) − (2x² + x − 6).
items.explanation: Distribute the negative: 5x² − 3x + 4 − 2x² − x + 6. Combine: 3x² − 4x + 10.

commonErrors.why: Changed the signs of the first two terms but not the constant.
Added the quadratics instead of subtracting.
Did not distribute the subtraction, so the signs of x and −6 stayed the same.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A quadratic function has zeros at x = −3 and x = 5. Which could be its equation?
items.explanation: A zero at x = r comes from a factor (x − r). So x = −3 gives (x + 3) and x = 5 gives (x − 5).

commonErrors.why: Used the zeros as the constants in the factors without reversing the signs.
Reversed the sign for −3 but not for 5.
Reversed the sign for 5 but not for −3.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The quadratic function g(x) = x² + bx − 24 has a zero at x = 3. What is its other zero?
items.explanation: The zeros multiply to −24. Since one zero is 3, the other is −24 ÷ 3 = −8. Then g(x) = (x − 3)(x + 8) = x² + 5x − 24.

commonErrors.why: Multiplied −24 by 3 instead of dividing.
Found the right size but dropped the negative sign.
Added 3 to −24 instead of using the product of the zeros.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Maya has $45 and saves $8 each week. Which equation can be solved to find the number of weeks w until she has $125?
items.explanation: Her money is the starting $45 plus $8 for each of w weeks, so 45 + 8w = 125.

commonErrors.why: Swapped the starting amount and the weekly savings.
Swapped the goal and the starting amount.
Left out the $45 she already has.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A club has at most $600 for a trip. The bus costs $150 flat plus $12 for each student. What is the greatest whole number of students who can go?
items.explanation: The inequality is 150 + 12s ≤ 600, so 12s ≤ 450 and s ≤ 37.5. Only whole students count, so the most is 37.

commonErrors.why: Rounded 37.5 up, which would exceed the budget.
Divided 600 by 12 and ignored the bus cost.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A rectangle's length is 3 more than its width w. Its area is 54 square units. Which equation can be solved to find w?
items.explanation: Area is length times width: (w + 3)(w) = 54, which expands to w² + 3w − 54 = 0.

commonErrors.why: Squared w but did not multiply the 3 by w.
Added the sides, which would be related to the perimeter, not the area.
Used a length that is 3 less than the width.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A car is worth $5,000 and loses 20% of its value each year. Which equation can be solved to find the number of years t until it is worth $2,048?
items.explanation: Each year the car keeps 80% of its value, so the value after t years is 5000(0.8)ᵗ. Setting that equal to 2048 gives the equation. Here t = 4.

commonErrors.why: Used a linear model instead of repeated multiplication.
Used the 20% loss rate instead of the 80% that remains each year.
Used a growth factor for a decreasing value.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A plumber charges a $40 call fee plus $35 per hour. Which equation gives the total cost C for h hours of work?
items.explanation: The $35 depends on hours h, and the $40 is charged once, so C = 35h + 40.

commonErrors.why: Multiplied the hourly rate by the fee as well, which distributes incorrectly.
Added the fee to the rate and multiplied by hours.
Swapped the fee and the hourly rate.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A theater sells adult tickets for $9 and child tickets for $5. One show brings in $270 from a adult tickets and c child tickets. Which equation relates a and c?
items.explanation: Adult revenue is 9a and child revenue is 5c. Together they total $270: 9a + 5c = 270.

commonErrors.why: Set the revenue equal to the number of tickets instead of $270.
Attached the prices to the wrong ticket types.
Used the combined price 9 + 5 for every ticket.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The points (1, 7), (2, 10), and (3, 13) all lie on the line y = mx + b. What is y when x = 10?
items.explanation: Each step of 1 in x adds 3 to y, so m = 3. Then 7 = 3(1) + b gives b = 4. At x = 10, y = 3(10) + 4 = 34.

commonErrors.why: Multiplied the slope by 10 and left out the intercept b = 4.
Multiplied the first y-value 7 by 10 instead of using the equation.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A rocket is launched upward from a platform 100 feet high at 80 feet per second. Its height h in feet after t seconds is a quadratic in which gravity contributes −16t². Which equation models h?
items.explanation: A projectile model is h = −16t² + vt + h₀ with v = 80 and h₀ = 100, so h = −16t² + 80t + 100.

commonErrors.why: Made the starting height negative.
Swapped the initial velocity and the initial height.
Used a positive t² coefficient, but gravity pulls the rocket down.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A jar has 20 coins that are all nickels (n) and dimes (d). The coins are worth 160 cents in all. Which system models this?
items.explanation: The count equation is n + d = 20. A nickel is 5 cents and a dime is 10 cents, so 5n + 10d = 160.

commonErrors.why: Swapped the number of coins and the total value.
Swapped the values of a nickel and a dime.
Mixed dollars with cents in the value equation.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: At a fair, 3 adult tickets and 2 child tickets cost $42, and 2 adult tickets and 4 child tickets cost $44. Which system models the adult price a and the child price k?
items.explanation: Each purchase gives one equation: 3a + 2k = 42 and 2a + 4k = 44.

commonErrors.why: Swapped the numbers of adult and child tickets in both equations.
Swapped the quantities in the second equation only.
Swapped the two totals.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Plan A costs $20 to join plus $4 per session. Plan B costs $50 to join plus $1 per session. After how many sessions do the two plans cost the same?
items.explanation: Set 20 + 4s = 50 + s. Then 3s = 30, so s = 10. Both plans cost $60 at that point.

commonErrors.why: Found the difference in joining fees but did not divide by the 3 dollar difference in rates.
Added the fees and added the rates, then divided: 70 ÷ 5.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Rosa earns $12 per hour at a café (c hours) and $15 per hour tutoring (t hours). She wants to earn at least $180 and can work at most 14 hours total. Which system of inequalities models this?
items.explanation: Earnings must be at least 180: 12c + 15t ≥ 180. Hours must be at most 14: c + t ≤ 14.

commonErrors.why: Attached the pay rates to the wrong jobs.
Reversed the inequality for hours; she can work at most 14.
Reversed the inequality for earnings; she wants at least $180.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The area of a triangle is A = ½bh. Solve this formula for h.
items.explanation: Multiply both sides by 2 to get 2A = bh, then divide by b: h = 2A/b.

commonErrors.why: Multiplied by b instead of dividing by b.
Forgot to undo the ½.
Divided by 2 instead of multiplying by 2 to undo the ½.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The formula C = (5/9)(F − 32) converts Fahrenheit to Celsius. Solve it for F.
items.explanation: Multiply both sides by 9/5: (9/5)C = F − 32. Then add 32: F = (9/5)C + 32.

commonErrors.why: Moved the 32 with the wrong sign.
Added 32 to C before multiplying by 9/5.
Did not use the reciprocal 9/5 to undo multiplication by 5/9.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Simple interest gives a total amount A = P(1 + rt). Solve this formula for t.
items.explanation: Divide by P: A/P = 1 + rt. Subtract 1: A/P − 1 = rt, so t = (A − P)/(Pr).

commonErrors.why: Subtracted 1 from A rather than from A/P.
Divided by (1 + r) as if t were multiplied by it.
Divided only A by Pr and then subtracted 1.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A student solves 3x + 7 = 22 in two steps. Step 1: 3x = 15. Step 2: x = 5. Which pair of properties justifies Steps 1 and 2?
items.explanation: Step 1 subtracts 7 from both sides (22 − 7 = 15). Step 2 divides both sides by 3 (15 ÷ 3 = 5).
choices: Subtraction property of equality, then multiplication property of equality
Division property of equality, then subtraction property of equality
Subtraction property of equality, then division property of equality
Addition property of equality, then division property of equality
items.answer: Subtraction property of equality, then division property of equality

commonErrors.answer: Subtraction property of equality, then multiplication property of equality
commonErrors.why: Used multiplication in Step 2 when 3x = 15 is undone by dividing by 3.

commonErrors.answer: Division property of equality, then subtraction property of equality
commonErrors.why: Reversed the order in which the operations were applied.

commonErrors.answer: Addition property of equality, then division property of equality
commonErrors.why: Thought 7 was added to both sides in Step 1, but 7 was subtracted.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Ava solved 2(x − 3) = 10. Step 1: 2x − 3 = 10. Step 2: 2x = 13. Step 3: x = 6.5. Where is her first error?
items.explanation: The 2 must multiply both terms: 2(x − 3) = 2x − 6. Ava wrote 2x − 3, so the first error is in Step 1. The right solution is x = 8.
choices: There is no error, because 6.5 checks in the original equation
Step 1, where she did not multiply −3 by 2
Step 2, where she added 3 to both sides
items.answer: Step 1, where she did not multiply −3 by 2

commonErrors.answer: There is no error, because 6.5 checks in the original equation
commonErrors.why: Did not substitute to check: 2(6.5 − 3) = 7, not 10.
Believed dividing by 2 was wrong, but that step follows from Step 2.

commonErrors.answer: Step 2, where she added 3 to both sides
commonErrors.why: Believed adding 3 was wrong, but that step follows correctly from Step 1.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: To solve x² = 7x, a student divides both sides by x and gets x = 7. Which statement describes the problem with this method?
items.explanation: Dividing by x is not allowed when x could be 0. Instead, x² − 7x = 0 factors as x(x − 7) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 7.
choices: It should have taken the square root of both sides
It adds the extra solution x = −7
It is correct because 7 is the only solution

commonErrors.answer: It should have taken the square root of both sides
commonErrors.why: Believed square roots are needed, but that leads to a different, harder equation.

commonErrors.answer: It adds the extra solution x = −7
commonErrors.why: Thought dividing by x creates a negative root, but it does not.

commonErrors.answer: It is correct because 7 is the only solution
commonErrors.why: Did not check x = 0, which also satisfies x² = 7x.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: In solving 4(x + 2) = 3x + 15, a student writes 4x + 8 = 3x + 15. Which property justifies this step?
items.explanation: 4(x + 2) = 4·x + 4·2 = 4x + 8 by the distributive property.

commonErrors.why: Thought the factors were regrouped, but the 4 was multiplied across the sum.
Thought a number was added to both sides, but nothing was added to either side.
Thought order was changed, but no terms were reordered.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve 4x − 9 = 15.
items.explanation: Add 9 to both sides: 4x = 24. Divide by 4: x = 6.

commonErrors.why: Ignored the −9 and only divided 15 by 4.
Subtracted 9 from 15 instead of adding it.
Added 9 but forgot to divide by 4.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve 3(x − 2) = 5x + 4.
items.explanation: Distribute: 3x − 6 = 5x + 4. Move the x terms and constants: 3x − 5x = 4 + 6, so −2x = 10 and x = −5.

commonErrors.why: Did not multiply −2 by 3, writing 3x − 2 on the left.
Added 5x to the left side instead of subtracting.
Made a sign error and got 10 = 2x.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve x/2 + x/3 = 10 for x.
items.explanation: Use a common denominator of 6: 3x/6 + 2x/6 = 5x/6 = 10. Then x = 10 × 6/5 = 12.

commonErrors.why: Added the denominators to get x/5 = 10.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve −3x + 5 > 17.
items.explanation: Subtract 5: −3x > 12. Divide by −3 and reverse the inequality: x < −4.

commonErrors.why: Dropped the negative sign while dividing.
Dropped the negative sign and did not reverse the inequality.
Did not reverse the inequality when dividing by −3.

items.subject: math
items.explanation: Distribute: 5 − 2x − 2 ≥ 3x − 12, so 3 − 2x ≥ 3x − 12. Then 15 ≥ 5x, so x ≤ 3.

commonErrors.why: Distributed −2 as −2x + 2 instead of −2x − 2.
Reversed the inequality at the end even though the last division was by a positive number.
Moved 3x to the left side with the wrong sign.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve x² = 49. Which are all of the solutions?
items.explanation: Taking square roots gives x = ±√49 = ±7, so both 7 and −7 work.

commonErrors.why: Treated the right side as the solution without taking a square root.
Divided 49 by 2 instead of taking a square root.
Took only the positive square root.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve x² − 8x + 15 = 0 by factoring. Which are all of the solutions?

commonErrors.why: Did not reverse the signs from the factors (x − 3)(x − 5).
Picked a factor pair of 15 that does not add to −8.
Used the coefficients as the solutions.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve (x − 4)² = 25. Which are all of the solutions?
items.explanation: Take square roots: x − 4 = 5 or x − 4 = −5. So x = 9 or x = −1.

commonErrors.why: Subtracted 4 instead of adding 4 after taking the square root.
Added and subtracted 25 instead of taking its square root.
Used only the positive square root of 25.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve 4x² − 25 = 0. What is the positive solution? Enter a fraction or decimal.
items.explanation: Add 25: 4x² = 25. Divide by 4: x² = 25/4. Take the square root: x = ±5/2, so the positive solution is 5/2.

commonErrors.why: Stopped at x² = 25/4 and did not take a square root.
Took the square root of 25 but not of 4.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The equation 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0 has two solutions. What is the larger one? Enter a fraction or decimal.
items.explanation: Factor: 2x² + 5x − 3 = (2x − 1)(x + 3) = 0. So x = 1/2 or x = −3, and the larger is 1/2.

commonErrors.why: Reversed the sign of the root x = −3.
Used the leading coefficient instead of solving 2x − 1 = 0.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve x(x − 5) = 14. Which are all of the solutions?
items.explanation: Expand and set to zero: x² − 5x − 14 = 0, which factors as (x − 7)(x + 2) = 0. So x = 7 or x = −2.

commonErrors.why: Set each factor equal to 14, which does not work when the product is not zero.
Changed the sign of the factor (x + 2) when solving.
Reversed the signs on the factors of x² − 5x − 14 = (x − 7)(x + 2).

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve the system by substitution: y = 2x + 1 and 3x + y = 11. What is the solution (x, y)?
items.explanation: Substitute: 3x + (2x + 1) = 11, so 5x = 10 and x = 2. Then y = 2(2) + 1 = 5.

commonErrors.why: Swapped the order of x and y when writing the answer.
Found x = 2 correctly but used y = 2x − 1 to get y.
Found x = 2 but substituted into y = 3x + 1.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve the system by elimination: x + y = 9 and x − y = 3. What is the solution (x, y)?
items.explanation: Adding the equations gives 2x = 12, so x = 6. Then y = 9 − 6 = 3.

commonErrors.why: Found x = 6 correctly but computed y = 3 − 6 instead of 9 − 6.
Swapped x and y in the answer.
Added the equations to get 2x = 12 but forgot to divide by 2, then used y = 9 − 12.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A system has equations (A) 2x + y = 7 and (B) x − y = 2. Equation (A) is replaced by the sum of (A) and (B). What is the new equation?
items.explanation: Adding left sides: 2x + y + x − y = 3x. Adding right sides: 7 + 2 = 9. The new equation is 3x = 9, and it has the same solution as the original system.

commonErrors.why: Subtracted the equations (A − B) instead of adding them.
Added the x terms and constants but wrote +y + y = 2y instead of cancelling +y and −y.
Added the left sides correctly but subtracted the right sides.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve the system x + 2y = 11 and x = 3y − 4. What is the value of y?
items.explanation: Substitute x = 3y − 4: 3y − 4 + 2y = 11, so 5y = 15 and y = 3.

commonErrors.why: That is x, not y.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: At a school play, 3 adult tickets and 2 student tickets cost $37. 2 adult tickets and 4 student tickets cost $38. What is the price of one student ticket?
items.explanation: Multiply the first equation by 2: 6a + 4s = 74. Subtract the second: 4a = 36, so a = 9. Then 27 + 2s = 37, so s = 5.

commonErrors.why: Eliminated adult tickets correctly to get 2s = 10 but forgot to divide by 2.
Reported the price of one adult plus one student ticket.
Reported the adult ticket price instead of the student price.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: How many solutions does this system have? 2x − 4y = 6 and x − 2y = 5
items.explanation: Multiply the second equation by 2: 2x − 4y = 10. Compared with 2x − 4y = 6 this is a contradiction, so the parallel lines never meet.

commonErrors.why: Saw matching x and y coefficients and decided the lines are the same.
Did not notice elimination settles it algebraically.
Assumed two different equations must cross at one point.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: For what value of k does the system 3x + ky = 12 and x + 2y = 4 have infinitely many solutions?
items.explanation: Multiplying x + 2y = 4 by 3 gives 3x + 6y = 12, which is the first equation when k = 6. The equations then describe the same line.

commonErrors.why: Matched k to the constant on the right of the second equation.
Copied the y coefficient of the second equation without scaling.
Matched k to the x coefficient of the first equation.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve the system 3x + 4y = 1 and 2x + 5y = −4. What is the solution (x, y)?
items.explanation: Multiply the first by 2 and the second by 3: 6x + 8y = 2 and 6x + 15y = −12. Subtract: 7y = −14, so y = −2. Then 3x − 8 = 1 gives x = 3.

commonErrors.why: Found y = −2 but forgot to divide by 3 when solving 3x = 9.
Swapped x and y in the answer.
Lost the negative sign on y after finding 7y = −14.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: In the system x + y = 5 and x − y = 1, the second equation is replaced by the sum of the two equations. Why does the new system have the same solution?
items.explanation: A pair satisfying both equations satisfies their sum. Subtracting the first equation from the sum gives the replaced equation back, so the solution sets match.
choices: The sum of two equations has the same graph as each of the original lines
Adding equations always cancels a variable, so the solution stays fixed
Old solutions satisfy the sum, and subtraction recovers the old equation
Adding creates new solutions, which shifts the point where the lines meet
items.answer: Old solutions satisfy the sum, and subtraction recovers the old equation

commonErrors.answer: The sum of two equations has the same graph as each of the original lines
commonErrors.why: Confused the sum with the original lines; it is a different line.

commonErrors.answer: Adding equations always cancels a variable, so the solution stays fixed
commonErrors.why: Believed cancelling a variable is the reason; it is only a convenience.

commonErrors.answer: Adding creates new solutions, which shifts the point where the lines meet
commonErrors.why: Thought adding changes the solution instead of preserving it.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Two functions are given by tables. x: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. f(x) = x + 2: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. g(x) = 3x − 4: −4, −1, 2, 5, 8. What is the solution of the system y = x + 2 and y = 3x − 4?
items.explanation: Both functions equal 5 at x = 3, so the graphs meet at (3, 5). Check: 3 + 2 = 5 and 3(3) − 4 = 5.

commonErrors.why: Read f(2) = 4 and did not check that g(2) = 2.
Swapped x and y when reading the matching row.
Used the g(x) value from x = 4 instead of finding where both match.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Solve the system x/2 + y/3 = 7 and 2x − y = 7. What is the solution (x, y)?
items.explanation: Multiply the first equation by 6: 3x + 2y = 42. From the second, y = 2x − 7, so 3x + 4x − 14 = 42, giving x = 8 and y = 9.

commonErrors.why: Swapped x and y in the answer.

items.explanation: Predicted ŷ = 1.5(10) + 8 = 23. Residual = 21 − 23 = −2.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A line is fit to data at x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. The residuals (actual − predicted) are 6, 1, −3, −4, −3, 0, 3. What do they suggest?
items.explanation: The residuals go positive, then negative, then positive again. A random scatter would support a line; this curved pattern shows the data are curved.
choices: Some are small, so a line fits well
A U-shaped pattern, so a line is not a good model
They add to 0, so a line fits well
The line is too steep, so the slope should be lowered
items.answer: A U-shaped pattern, so a line is not a good model

commonErrors.answer: Some are small, so a line fits well
commonErrors.why: Judged fit from a few small residuals and ignored the pattern.

commonErrors.answer: They add to 0, so a line fits well
commonErrors.why: Treated a zero total as proof of fit, but least-squares residuals always add to 0.

commonErrors.answer: The line is too steep, so the slope should be lowered
commonErrors.why: Mistook a curved residual pattern for a slope error.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Points (1, 3), (2, 5) and (3, 8) are compared with two lines. Model A: ŷ = 2.5x + 0.5. Model B: ŷ = 2x + 1. Which model has the smaller sum of squared residuals, and what are the two sums?
items.explanation: Model A predicts 3, 5.5, 8, with residuals 0, −0.5, 0 and sum of squares 0.25. Model B predicts 3, 5, 7, with residuals 0, 0, 1 and sum of squares 1. The smaller sum is the better fit.
choices: Model A: 0.5 versus 1 for Model B
Model B: 0 versus 0.25 for Model A
Model A: 0.25 versus 1 for Model B
Model B: 1 versus 0.25 for Model A
items.answer: Model A: 0.25 versus 1 for Model B

commonErrors.answer: Model A: 0.5 versus 1 for Model B
commonErrors.why: Added the residuals' sizes without squaring the −0.5.

commonErrors.answer: Model B: 0 versus 0.25 for Model A
commonErrors.why: Counted only B's zero residuals and overlooked its residual of 1.

commonErrors.answer: Model B: 1 versus 0.25 for Model A
commonErrors.why: Matched the sums correctly but picked the larger one as better.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The least-squares line ŷ = 2.4x + 15 predicts the number of free throws made out of 50 (y) from weekly practice hours (x). What does the slope 2.4 mean?
items.explanation: The slope is the change in predicted y for each 1-unit increase in x, here 2.4 free throws per hour.
choices: Each extra practice hour adds about 2.4 predicted free throws.
A player who never practices is predicted to make 2.4 shots.
Each extra free throw made adds about 2.4 practice hours.
Each extra practice hour adds about 15 predicted free throws.
items.answer: Each extra practice hour adds about 2.4 predicted free throws.

commonErrors.answer: A player who never practices is predicted to make 2.4 shots.
commonErrors.why: Mixed up the slope with the intercept.

commonErrors.answer: Each extra free throw made adds about 2.4 practice hours.
commonErrors.why: Reversed the roles of the variables.

commonErrors.answer: Each extra practice hour adds about 15 predicted free throws.
commonErrors.why: Used the intercept as the rate of change.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The line ŷ = 3.2x + 52 was fit to test scores (y, out of 100) for students who studied from 0 to 8 hours (x). A student plans to study 20 hours. Which evaluation is best?
items.explanation: ŷ = 3.2(20) + 52 = 116. That is extrapolation well beyond the 0 to 8 hour data, and a score over 100 is impossible, so the prediction is not trustworthy.
choices: Predicts 116, which is not valid: 20 is far outside the data and scores top out at 100.
Predicts 116, which is valid: a line works for any number of hours studied.
Predicts 64, which is a reasonable value for a score, so the model is fine.
Predicts 116, which is valid: studying more always raises a score.
items.answer: Predicts 116, which is not valid: 20 is far outside the data and scores top out at 100.

commonErrors.why: Assumed a linear model can be extended without limit.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A scatter plot looks curved. A line fit to the data has r = 0.93, but its residual plot shows a clear U shape. What is the best conclusion?
items.explanation: A high r only measures how close the data are to a line overall. A patterned residual plot shows a systematic misfit, so a nonlinear model is better.
choices: 93% of the points lie exactly on the fitted line.
The U shape shows that the correlation must be negative, not positive.
A line is appropriate for these data, because r is close to 1.
A line is not appropriate even though r is high; a curve fits better.
items.answer: A line is not appropriate even though r is high; a curve fits better.

commonErrors.answer: 93% of the points lie exactly on the fitted line.
commonErrors.why: Read r as the percent of points on the line.

commonErrors.answer: The U shape shows that the correlation must be negative, not positive.
commonErrors.why: Mistook a residual pattern for the sign of r.

commonErrors.answer: A line is appropriate for these data, because r is close to 1.
commonErrors.why: Used r alone and ignored the residual pattern.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: Over 30 summer days, a beach town finds that daily ice cream sales and daily sunburn cases have a correlation of r = 0.88. Which conclusion is best supported?
items.explanation: A hidden factor, hot sunny weather, can drive both variables. Correlation shows association, not causation.
choices: The strong correlation proves that no other factor is involved at all.
Ice cream sales cause people to get sunburns.
Both rise on hot, sunny days; the data do not show that one causes the other.
Sunburns cause people to buy more ice cream cones.
items.answer: Both rise on hot, sunny days; the data do not show that one causes the other.

commonErrors.answer: The strong correlation proves that no other factor is involved at all.
commonErrors.why: Believed a high r rules out a lurking variable.

commonErrors.answer: Ice cream sales cause people to get sunburns.
commonErrors.why: Treated a strong correlation as proof that one variable causes the other.

commonErrors.answer: Sunburns cause people to buy more ice cream cones.
commonErrors.why: Reversed the cause and effect, still assuming causation.
